releaseStatus.source: UKHSA, Reports of cases of TB to UK enhanced tuberculosis surveillance systems: quality and methodology information, 4 September 2025

measure: People notified with TB disease, by area of residence and calendar year of notification. Local figures are three-year averages of the annual count and of the rate per 100,000.
denominatorNotes: Note 1: CI denotes 'confidence interval'. A confidence interval indicates the likely range in which an estimated parameter (such as a mean or rate) is likely to fall. A 95% confidence interval indicates that if we repeated the study many times, 95% of the confidence intervals would contain the true population value.
Note 2: Population estimates for 2025 were taken from 2024.
Note 1: Population estimates for UK born and non-UK born were from 2024 data as 2025 data was unavailable.

Note 2: CI denotes confidence interval. A confidence interval indicates the likely range in which an estimated parameter (such as a mean or rate) is likely to fall. A 95% confidence interval indicates that if we repeated the study many times, 95% of the confidence intervals would contain the true population value.
caveat: TB notifications are not arrivals data. Local rates are averages over 2023 to 2025, so they are not comparable with England's single-year rate. England only: Welsh areas have no rate here. UKHSA publishes Hackney with the City of London, and Cornwall with the Isles of Scilly, as combined areas, so neither half is shown with a rate of its own. Areas absent from UKHSA's table have no rate.
